answer: Listen for shared silence. A farm runs its fifty identities on one box, so when the box hiccups they all go quiet in the same hour. The ledger keeps each identity's missed epochs as a bit string; identities whose gaps line up far beyond chance over 30 epochs are paid as one. Honest agents fail at their own odd times, scattered like raven tracks on the tundra. Hiding costs real money: separate machines, power and networks, or the hollow hours give the farm away. Assumption: co-hosted honest agents can appeal by proving separate operators.
